summary.intent: Execute Phase 27 (writable-shares-poc) end-to-end: implement API backend, owner UI, and recipient UI for write-enabled sharing with UAT checkpoint, then perform a security review and fix all identified issues.
summary.outcome: Phase 27 fully executed with 3 plans across 3 waves, UAT completed with 4 in-session bug fixes, 8 security issues fixed using TDD (red→green), 21 E2E tests written and passing, all changes committed and pushed to feat/phase-27-writable-shares.

repo: The cipher-box-ci-debug checkout does not share .env files with the main cipher-box repo — they must be copied manually when the DB host changes or on fresh checkouts
VITE_API_URL must be set explicitly in apps/web/.env; the fallback uses window.location.origin+'/api' which incorrectly points to the web port (5173) instead of the API port (3000)
The SDK dependency chain for the web app requires building in order: @cipherbox/core → @cipherbox/sdk-core → @cipherbox/sdk before the web dev server can start

Auth controller defined its own local RequestWithUser interface extending NestJS @nestjs/common Request (Fetch API) instead of the shared common/types.ts one extending Express Request, causing type incompatibility in specs

The writable-shares upload flow requires dual IPNS key wrapping: FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted must use the owner's key (so owner can update), while the recipient gets a separate file-ipns share_key entry
withConflictRetry closures in useSharedNavigation.ts capture stale React state — refs (folderChildrenRef, sequenceNumberRef) must be synced alongside state setters for use inside closures
The ShareDialog downgrade flow used .share-revoke-confirm-btn--yes for confirmation, same selector as full revocation
SharedFileBrowser uses an inline input (.shared-inline-input-field) for mkdir rather than a modal CreateFolderDialog
SharedFileBrowser uses .shared-inline-rename-field for rename inline editing
The recipient-permission label classes are recipient-perm-write and recipient-perm-read, not share-recipient-permission

code.finding: Original shared upload set fileMetaIpnsName: '' — fixed by inlining full IPNS record creation with dual-key wrapping
withConflictRetry upload closure used stale React state; must use folderChildrenRef.current and sequenceNumberRef.current
Save path used owner's useFolder hook (updateFile); shared files need a separate onSaveSharedFile callback prop routed through SharedFileBrowser
handleUpdateFile did not re-wrap the new file key for share recipients after owner edits — reWrapForRecipients must be called after every file content update
updatePermission (downgrade path) did not delete file-ipns share_keys, leaving recipients able to modify file metadata after revocation
keyType enum needed 'file-ipns' added for storing recipient-wrapped IPNS private keys separately from file content keys
Falls back to window.location.origin+'/api' when VITE_API_URL is not set — this is wrong when API and web run on different ports
Imported Request from @nestjs/common (Fetch API) and defined local RequestWithUser; should import RequestWithUser from common/types.ts which extends Express Request

workflow: Background bash tasks in Claude Code are killed when conversation context shifts — use detached processes (nohup or disown) for dev servers that must survive
TDD red→green flow: stash fixes, write failing tests against unfixed code, verify they fail, pop stash, verify tests go green — ensures tests actually validate the fix
NestJS watch mode does not always pick up DTO @ApiProperty enum changes for OpenAPI spec generation; full server restart required before regenerating API client
When an API client is regenerated, TypeScript checks may still show old enum values if the server wasn't running with updated code during generation
E2E tests for IPNS-dependent flows need explicit page reloads and generous timeouts due to IPNS propagation delays between writer and reader
Security reviews should check both the intent of the spec and the actual implementation — several issues (H-01, M-01, L-03) were already correctly implemented

friction: DB host IP changed mid-session (192.168.133.114 → 192.168.133.12), requiring .env recreation from .env.example with manual IP substitution
Background task kills repeatedly interrupted dev server restarts — needed 3+ attempts before switching to detached processes
cipher-box-ci-debug had no .env files; web app silently fell back to wrong API URL causing 'disconnected' status with no clear error
NestJS OpenAPI spec didn't update after DTO change until full server restart, blocking API client regeneration
Git lock file interference required manual removal mid-commit sequence

E2E test selector mismatches on first run: recipient-perm-write vs share-recipient-permission, shared-inline-input-field vs folder-name-input, shared-inline-rename-field vs file-name-input — required screenshot-driven correction
The backend security fix agent ran in parallel with frontend work, requiring stash/pop coordination to maintain TDD ordering
Pre-existing TypeScript errors in auth and device-approval controller specs unrelated to phase 27 work surfaced during compilation checks and required investigation and fixing
open_items: E2E tests cover the happy path for writable shares but silent revocation (30s polling detecting permission changes) and the full revocation-to-read-only transition are marked as hard to test manually and not fully automated

The reWrapForRecipients call in useFileOperations.ts is a post-hoc fix — the owner file update flow has no mechanism to handle files shared with multiple recipients with different key types; needs audit if multi-recipient write shares are introduced
Subfolder key wrapping for C-02 fix adds a recipient share_key for the immediate subfolder but does not recursively handle nested subfolders created inside that subfolder
The 'file-ipns' keyType in share_keys is stored with an 'as any' cast in the delete call — the entity enum should be updated to include it properly in a follow-up
No PR created yet — the session ended after push with the question of whether to create a PR

The security review identified L-02 (BigInt sequence number coercion) as fixed but the implementation detail of how stale sequence numbers interact with multi-writer concurrent edits at the protocol level was not fully validated
